authorReviewNote: Seven normal full-team netball count, not five/six/nine. World Netball current rules introduction explicitly two teams of seven. Removed seven-a-side from stem because it gave away answer. Standard rulebook qualifier excludes Fast5 and team may be temporarily reduced.

GS and GA permitted shooters; other offered position pairs include no permitted shooter. Actual World Netball scoring and playing-ball sections checked, only GS/GA in goal circle. Does not imply may shoot from anywhere or all competition formats have identical points zones.

Backboard absent, ring/net/post present. World Netball technical goalpost specifications list pole, ring, projecting bar and net; basketball comparison familiar. Normally qualifier allows adapted informal equipment, no assertion every basketball basket is pole-mounted.

Three seconds normal holding time, not one/five/ten. Actual World Netball playing-ball rule4 explicitly possession release by pass/shot within3seconds, not just centre-pass special rule. No claim stopped play counts same as active possession.

Pivot permitted with landing foot grounded. Running/repeated forward hops/dribbling not allowed footwork. Actual rulebook pivot definition inspected, clear landing-foot condition. Avoided claim pivot mandatory or lifted landing foot can freely be replaced before release.

Indoor handball normal seven including goalkeeper. IOC actual how-many-players paragraph confirms seven, permits fewer to start but question normal full team. Five/eight/eleven not standard count. Scope indoor avoids beach/old field handball.

Three steps normal ball-held movement without dribble. IOC actual how-to paragraph explicit max3steps; one/five/seven wrong limit. No teaching of detailed foot-contact exceptions. Normally excludes unusual officiating sequences.

Three seconds normal stationary holding limit. IOC actual how-to paragraph explicit possession maximum3seconds. One/eight/ten wrong; without playing it excludes active dribbling. Plain grammar, distinct from three-steps movement question.

Throw ball into opponent goal, not crossbar kick/hole strike/endline carry. IOC actual objective/scoring explanation inspected. Distinct equipment/game objectives all plausible sports; does not claim every throw succeeds or every contact is hands-only.

Goalkeeper normally stands to defend in own goal area; other defender/captain/substitute role alone does not permit it. Actual IHF6.1 and6.3 indexed text inspected, including non-advantageous encroachment exceptions. Replaced insufficient IOCarea reference with exact IHF rule. Normally permits role switches and does not forbid airborne jump shots.
First11 with two-point margin, not7/15/21. Actual ITTF2026 law2.11.1 inspected. Explicit margin avoids claiming a10allgame ends11-10. Standard game not match, so does not confuse best-of games.

Serve first bounces own court then directly receiver court. ITTF2026law2.6.3 actual passage checked. Floor/receiver-racket/sidewall wrong. Singles scope avoids required diagonal right-half doubles nuance; no claim serve hitting net always automatically out.

Alternating partners under standing-player doubles. ITTF2026law2.8.2 and wheelchair exception2.8.3 both inspected. Added standing scope rather than ignoring actual disabled-pair variation. Either partner/every shot/server only/together wrong ordinary sequence.

Net divides two halves; glass/wood/pegs not table-tennis divider. ITTF2026 net assembly and service playing-surface rules checked. Familiar accessible equipment fact, not borrowing a tennis net's dimensions.

Replaced trivial racket function with legal striking-face covering: rubber (ordinary pimpled or sandwich). ITTF2026law2.4.3 actually inspected. Baremetal/leather/cork not allowed striking face; does not falsely say entire wooden blade is rubber.

Bouldering short indoor rope-free routes over mats, not lead/abseil/ice. BMC competition definition1.1.1 and landingmat1.2.1 actual indexed text checked. Indoor wording avoids claiming every outdoor boulder has matting; no how-to safety instructions.

Belayer manages safety rope, not paint/scorecard/other competitors' timings. BMC actual belaying definition describes loaded rope and taking slack; gear page confirms safeguarding partner. No claim one generic procedure works for every belay device.

Carabiner connects safety-system parts. BMC actual quickdraw guide describes two karabiners joining sling/rope/protection. Height-measuring/hand-drying/difficulty-marking wrong functions. No claim all hardware clips suitable for climbing or guaranteed fall prevention.

Chalk absorbs hand moisture, not hold-softening/rope lubricant/complete fingertip protection. Actual BMC gear guide explicitly sweat absorption inspected. Avoided categorical promise chalk always improves friction in every condition; purpose fact clear.

Lead climber clips rope into protection while ascending. Actual BMC quickdraw guide opening explicitly rope/protection in lead climbing. Coiled-unused/measuring/tying around handholds wrong procedures. General concept only; not replacing instruction in safety skills.

Sculler two oars, alternatives1/3/4 wrong per athlete. World Rowing actual para-event explainer explicitly two oars per rower; also beginner booklet. Not total crew oars, not confused with two-person double boat.

Sweep rower one oar, not2/3/4. Same World Rowing actual distinction explicit; traditional two rowing categories paired facts but not duplicate as their oar allocation differs. No suggestion crew size must be one.

Coxswain steers/coaches crew, doesn't row every stroke/judge other boats/swim behind. World Rowing learn-to-row booklet actual boat-types passage explicitly coach and steer. Coxed qualifier avoids implying every boat carries one or every cox sits astern.

Rowers conventionally face backward relative travel. British Rowing/PaddleUK actual navigation guidance indexed passage explicitly rowers face backwards and use oars. Other directions false normal racing. Does not imply coxswain faces backward or every rowing adaptation identical.

Rowing ergometer off-water rowing simulation, not treadmill/bicycle/skilift. Actual World Rowing indoor-rowing article explicit training ergometer and rowing action. Doesn't deny other exercise machines can improve fitness; question specific simulation.
